q: At what temperature does water freeze in degrees Celsius?
fact: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.
why_false: 40 degrees Celsius is a hot summer temperature; water is liquid there, not ice.

q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
fact: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
why_false: 400 degrees Celsius is four times the boiling point; water is steam long before that.

q: Why does ice take up more space than the liquid water it came from?
fact: Water expands as it freezes, so ice takes up more room than the liquid.
why_false: Water does not shrink on freezing; if it did, ice would sink and pipes would not burst.

q: How long does it take for light to travel from the Sun to Earth?
fact: Light takes about eight minutes to cross from the Sun to Earth.
why_false: Sixty minutes is more than seven times the real delay.

q: What percentage of air is nitrogen?
fact: Air is roughly 78 percent nitrogen.
why_false: At 18 percent nitrogen the remaining four fifths of the air would be unaccounted for; nitrogen is the majority component.

q: What color and state is sulfur at room temperature?
fact: Sulfur is a bright yellow solid.
why_false: Sulfur is not purple; its yellow colour is one of its best-known properties.

q: Why does stone feel colder than wood at the same temperature?
fact: Stone conducts heat away from skin faster than wood, which is why it feels colder at the same temperature.
why_false: If rock carried heat away more slowly than timber, a stone floor would feel warmer than a wooden one, which it does not.

q: What happens to molten metal as it cools in a casting form?
fact: Molten metal solidifies as it cools in a casting form.
why_false: Iron does not boil away into steam as it cools; steam is water, and cooling metal freezes rather than evaporates.

q: Which is flammable, cotton or steel?
fact: Cotton is flammable; steel is not.
why_false: Paper burns at least as easily as cotton, so it is not the non-flammable case.

q: What gas is used to carbonate fizzy drinks?
fact: Fizzy drinks are carbonated with dissolved carbon dioxide.
why_false: Carbon monoxide is a poison and is not used to carbonate drinks.

q: Why is lightning seen before thunder is heard?
fact: Light travels vastly faster than sound, so lightning is seen before thunder is heard.
why_false: If light were slower than sound the thunder would arrive first, which never happens.

q: Which is denser, iron or wood?
fact: Iron is much denser than wood.
why_false: Lead is considerably denser than iron, so the comparison is backwards.

q: What color does litmus paper turn when exposed to acids?
fact: Acids turn litmus paper red.
why_false: Blue is what litmus turns in a base; acid does the opposite.

q: How does the Sun produce light and energy?
fact: The Sun shines by fusing hydrogen into helium.
why_false: Fission splits heavy nuclei; joining hydrogen into helium is by definition not fission.

q: What happens to the pressure of a fixed volume of air when it is heated?
fact: Heating a fixed volume of air raises its pressure.
why_false: Loudness is a property of sound, not something heating trapped air produces.

q: What type of energy does a torch use from its battery?
fact: A torch runs on chemical energy stored in its battery.
why_false: Plastic is inert casing material and stores no usable chemical energy for the device.

q: Why does gold not tarnish over time?
fact: Gold is chemically very unreactive, so it does not tarnish.
why_false: Gold is one of the most valuable metals, not one of the least, and value would not explain the shine anyway.

q: What does the magnetic field do to the solar wind from the Sun?
fact: The magnetic field deflects the solar wind, a stream of charged particles from the Sun.
why_false: The Moon emits no wind of particles; it has neither the atmosphere nor the output to do so.

q: Why does cool air sink compared to warm air?
fact: Cool air is denser and therefore heavier than warm air, so it sinks.
why_false: If cool air were lighter it would rise, and cold air would collect at the ceiling instead of the floor.

q: What is burning chemically defined as?
fact: Burning is combination with oxygen.
why_false: Helium is a noble element that does not burn or support burning.

q: Can sound travel through a vacuum?
fact: Sound needs a medium and cannot travel through a vacuum.
why_false: Sound travels through a planet perfectly well; earthquakes are detected worldwide that way.

q: What causes static electricity when surfaces come into contact?
fact: Static electricity comes from transfer of electrons between surfaces.
why_false: Rubbing does not tear whole molecules off a fabric; static charge is carried by electrons.

q: What force is required for circular motion and in which direction does it act?
fact: Circular motion requires a centripetal force directed toward the axis.
why_false: An upward force cannot bend motion into a circle; the rim would fly off tangentially.

q: Why is an aluminium can lighter than a steel one?
fact: Aluminium is much less dense than steel, so an aluminium can is lighter than a steel one.
why_false: Paper is far lighter than any metal, so the metal can is not lighter than a paper one.

q: Why do iron frames rust but aluminium ones do not?
fact: Rust is iron oxide; iron frames rust and aluminium ones do not.
why_false: Wood does not rust at all, so it cannot be the contrast case for rusting.

q: Who made the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903?
fact: The Wright brothers made the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903.
why_false: 1803 predates the internal combustion engine by decades; no powered flight was possible then.

q: What is diesel refined from?
fact: Diesel is a fuel refined from crude oil (petroleum).
why_false: Limestone is a rock used for cement and building stone; no liquid fuel is refined from it.

q: How did early steam locomotives generate steam?
fact: Early steam locomotives raised steam by burning coal in a firebox.
why_false: Sand does not burn at all; it was carried for traction, not as fuel.

q: What greenhouse gas is mainly produced by burning hydrocarbon fuels in car exhaust?
fact: Burning a hydrocarbon fuel produces carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas in car exhaust.
why_false: Car exhaust contains no carbon chloride; chlorine is not present in the fuel or the air being burned.

q: What part of a car engine do pistons move inside?
fact: Pistons in a car engine move inside cylinders.
why_false: A battery is a sealed store of electrical energy; nothing slides inside it.

q: What tool is carried to lift a car when changing a wheel?
fact: A jack is the tool carried to lift a car when changing a wheel.
why_false: A mat cannot lift anything; it is a floor covering.

q: What is the structure of laminated safety glass?
fact: Laminated safety glass sandwiches a thin plastic interlayer between two glass sheets.
why_false: Granite is an opaque rock; a slab of it between two sheets of glass would make the panel impossible to see through.

q: What are pneumatic bicycle tyres inflated with?
fact: Pneumatic bicycle tyres are inflated with air.
why_false: Bicycle tyres are not filled with oil; a liquid is essentially incompressible and would give no cushioning.

q: What power source do London's underground trains use from the rails?
fact: London's underground trains run on electric power drawn from live rails.
why_false: Waterwheels are fixed installations driven by a stream; no train has ever been driven by one.

q: Are there sections of the German Autobahn with no mandatory speed limit?
fact: Large parts of the German Autobahn have no mandatory speed limit.
why_false: Every road has a fixed width, and vehicle width limits apply throughout Germany; there is no such thing as a road with no width limit.

q: What do traction lifts hang from that is wound over a driven sheave or drum?
fact: Traction lifts hang from steel cables wound over a driven sheave or drum.
why_false: A sponge is soft and absorbent and cannot be made of steel or bear a load.

q: What does a battery do with chemical energy during discharge?
fact: A battery stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy on discharge.
why_false: Batteries hold no magnetic store of energy; they work by chemical reactions between their electrodes.

q: Why do aircraft structures use aluminium instead of steel?
fact: Aluminium is about a third the density of steel, which is why aircraft structures use it.
why_false: Aluminium is far less dense than steel, so it cannot be heavier for the same volume.

q: How does optical fibre transmit data along its glass core?
fact: Optical fibre transmits data as pulses of light guided along a glass core.
why_false: No data cable carries pulses of water; the fibre core is solid glass.

q: How tall is the Eiffel Tower including its antennas?
fact: The Eiffel Tower is roughly 330 m tall including its antennas.
why_false: 930 m would make it far taller than the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world.

q: Why do data centres require cooling systems according to energy usage by computer chips?
fact: Almost all the electrical power drawn by computer chips ends up as waste heat, which is why data centres need cooling.
why_false: No electrical device converts electricity into gold; elements cannot be created in a chip.

q: What are the first six letters on the top row of a standard English keyboard?
fact: The standard English keyboard layout starts its top letter row with Q, W, E, R, T, Y.
why_false: Standard keyboards are not laid out in alphabetical order; that arrangement was rejected long ago.

q: What propellants did the upper stages of the Saturn V use?
fact: The upper stages of the Saturn V burned liquid hydrogen with liquid oxygen.
why_false: Nitrogen does not burn; it is chemically inert in rocket engines and is used only as a pressurising gas.

q: What type of waves are radio waves and how fast do they travel?
fact: Radio waves are electromagnetic and propagate at the speed of light.
why_false: Sound is about a million times slower than light and cannot travel through the vacuum of space at all.

q: What causes the piston to move when water boils?
fact: Water expands roughly a thousandfold in volume when it boils, and that expansion drives the piston.
why_false: Boiling changes no mass at all; the same water weighs exactly the same as steam.

q: When did standardised container shipping begin with Malcom McLean's first container voyage?
fact: Standardised container shipping began in the mid-1950s with Malcom McLean's first container voyage.
why_false: The 1750s predate steel making on any industrial scale and predate powered cranes and lorries entirely.

q: What innovation by Henry Ford in 1913 drastically reduced Model T production time?
fact: Henry Ford's moving assembly line, introduced in 1913, cut the time to build a Model T dramatically.
why_false: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone and had nothing to do with car manufacturing.

q: What feature allows tanks to spread their weight over soft ground?
fact: Tanks run on continuous tracks, which spread their weight over soft ground.
why_false: Floats are buoyancy devices for aircraft and boats; no tank moves over land on them.

q: When did ARPANET, funded by the US Department of Defense, send its first message?
fact: ARPANET, funded by the US Department of Defense, sent its first message in 1969.
why_false: The 1860s predate the electronic computer by about eighty years.

q: What happens to the poured metal in sand casting before removing the sand?
fact: In sand casting the poured metal is left to cool and solidify before the sand is broken away.
why_false: The metal is already molten and is losing heat; it cannot boil, which would require thousands of degrees more.
